pl-l4d47c4-d1e115.summary: A heading encoded as a paragraph: 'On the order of the judgment and the ministry of angels'.

pl-l4d47c4-d1e118.summary: Notes that the Gospel says the Lord will send his angels to gather out of his kingdom all scandals and cast the wicked into the furnace of fire, and the angels will separate the wicked from among the just and cast them into the furnace (sentence continues).

pl-l4d47c4-d1e130.summary: Continues: and he will send his angels with a trumpet and they will gather the elect (sentence continues).

pl-l4d47c4-d1e137.summary: Completes: from the four winds; and the prophet says 'gather his saints to him'; there is no doubt these will be accomplished by the ministry of angels.
claims: The angels gather and separate at the judgment.

pl-l4d47c4-d1e146.summary: States that when the Lord comes to judgment a fire will go before him, by which the face of this world will be burned, and heaven and earth will perish not in substance but in appearance, which will be changed, the aerial heaven, not the ethereal; the fire will rise as high as the waters of the flood.
claims: The world-fire changes the world's appearance, not substance.
It affects the aerial heaven as far as the flood rose.

pl-l4d47c4-d1e149.summary: States that this fire will consume the wicked found alive, but not the good.
claims: The world-fire consumes the living wicked.

pl-l4d47c4-d1e152.summary: Cites Augustine: this burning of the world will be for the saints what the furnace was for the three youths; whatever needs purging in them will be purged by that fire; to others it will cause no harm.
claims: The world-fire purges the saints without harming them.

pl-l4d47c4-d1e158.summary: Describes the sequence: the world purged by fire and the Lord coming to judgment, the great voice will sound by which all the dead rise; then by the angels' ministry the floor will be winnowed, the good gathered from the four parts of the world and caught up to meet Christ in the air, the reprobate remaining on the earth they loved.
claims: The dead rise; angels gather the good to meet Christ; the reprobate remain on earth.

pl-l4d47c4-d1e164.summary: States that then the praises of the good, 'I was hungry and you fed me', and the rebukes of the wicked, 'I was hungry and you did not feed me', will be uttered, either by spoken sound or otherwise.

pl-l4d47c4-d1e174.summary: Concludes: finally the sentence will be pronounced on both, 'come, blessed' and 'depart, cursed', and by the angels' ministry, with God's power cooperating, the wicked will be cast into the furnace of fire, that is hell.
claims: After the sentence the wicked are cast into hell by angels.

pl-l4d47c4.summary: Under the heading on the order of judgment and the angels' ministry: the Gospel says the angels will gather scandals, separate the wicked from the just, and gather the elect from the four winds, so these will be done by angels. Before the Lord comes to judge, a fire will burn the face of this world, heaven and earth perishing in form, not substance, the aerial heaven, rising as high as the flood; it will consume the wicked found alive, but not the good, purging what needs purging in them, like the furnace of the three youths. Then the great voice will raise all the dead, the angels will winnow the floor, the good caught up to meet Christ and the reprobate left on earth, praises and rebukes will be uttered, the sentence pronounced, and the wicked sent by angels into hell.
claims: The angels minister at the judgment.
A fire will transform the world's appearance and purge the good.
The dead rise at the great voice and are separated by angels.
The wicked are sent into hell after the sentence.
